chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Abdul Rahman ibn Kathir, who said:

I fell sick in Medina, so my stomach went loose (diarrhea). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) prescribed for me the suweeq (parched grain flour) of javars (finger millet), and ordered me to take the suweeq of javars and drink it with cumin water. So I did so, and my stomach retained (stopped the loose motion), and I was healed.

key_terms.أَمْسَكَ بَطْنِي: Amsaka batni: My stomach retained/stopped (the loose motion).
key_terms.الْجَاوَرْس: Al-Jawars: Finger millet, a type of grain used in the remedy.
key_terms.سَوِيق: Suweeq: Parched grain flour, a traditional medicinal food.
key_terms.فَانْطَلَقَ بَطْنِي: Fantalqat batni: My stomach went loose (diarrhea).
key_terms.مَاءِ الْكَمُّون: Water of cumin: Cumin-infused water, used here for its digestive properties.

ai.seo_question: What was the traditional remedy for diarrhea prescribed by Imam Al-Sadiq (as)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the practical medical wisdom of Imam al-Sadiq (as), demonstrating the integration of dietary therapy with spiritual authority in Shia tradition. The specific combination of finger millet (*javors*) and cumin water illustrates the Prophetic tradition of utilizing natural, accessible remedies for gastrointestinal ailments, reinforcing the concept of *Tibb al-Nabawi* (Prophetic Medicine). It serves as a key reference for understanding how Imams provided both spiritual and physical guidance to their companions during times of illness.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said,

‘I fell sick at Al-Medina, so my stomach went (diarrhoea), so Abu Abdullahasws prescribed for me Al-Suweyq of the finger-millet and instructed me that I should take Al-Suweyq of the finger-millet and drink it with water of cumin. So I did it and my belly retained, and I regained health’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain persons of our people from Ali ibn Hassan from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Kathir who has said the following: “

I once became ill in al-Madinah because of diarrhea and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, described for me how to prepare a sawiq (fried flour) of al-Jawars and commanded me to use sawiq of al- Jawars and drink it with water of al-Kamun (cumin). I followed the instruction and the diarrhea stopped.’”
